# Use Meta AI to organize your next garage sale in 5 simple steps

By the end of this guide you’ll have a tidy inventory, sensible prices, and a printable flyer for your garage sale – all created with Meta AI, even if you’ve never written a line of code before.

## Before you start
- A free Meta account (you can sign up at meta.com).  
- Access to a web browser on a computer, tablet, or phone.  
- About 15 minutes total – you can pause between steps.  
- No paid plan is needed for the basic chat features used here.  

## Step 1 — Open Meta AI and start a new chat
Tap the **Chat** icon on the Meta homepage, then press the **+ New conversation** button. You’ll see a blank chat window with a text box at the bottom and a friendly greeting from the AI. The AI usually replies with “Hi! How can I help?” right away. If you don’t see a plus sign, look for a button that says **New chat** or a speech‑bubble icon at the top‑right of the page. 💬 Example: *“I’d like help planning a garage sale.”* You’ll know it worked when the AI responds with a brief outline of the planning steps.

## Step 2 — Ask Meta AI to create an item list template
In the chat box type a request for a simple spreadsheet‑style list of items you might sell. This is called a **prompt** (the instruction you give the AI). The AI will generate a table with columns like *Item*, *Condition*, and *Notes*. If the response looks like plain text instead of a table, ask the AI to “format it as a markdown table.” If the AI refuses, try re‑phrasing: “Can you show the list as a table with headings?” 💬 Example: *“Please give me a table with columns: Item, Condition, Notes.”* You’ll know it worked when you see a grid of rows and columns you can copy.

## Step 3 — Fill the list with your own items and set prices
Copy the table from the chat into a plain‑text editor (like Notepad) or directly into a spreadsheet program. Then type each item you plan to sell, adding a short description of its condition (e.g., *good*, *fair*, *like new*) and a suggested price. Meta AI can help you suggest prices – just ask, “What’s a fair price for a gently‑used toaster?” The AI will give a range based on typical second‑hand values. If the price seems too high, ask the AI for “lower‑end price suggestions.” 💬 Example: *“Suggest a price for a set of three ceramic mugs in good condition.”* You’ll know it worked when you have a completed list with a price next to every item.

## Step 4 — Turn the list into a flyer using Meta AI’s design prompt
Ask the AI to create a short flyer text that includes your garage‑sale date, time, address, and a highlight of the best items. This is called **generating content** – the AI writes the copy for you. The AI will return a block of text you can copy into a word‑processor or a free online flyer maker. If the AI’s output looks too long, say “Make the flyer description under 150 words.” If the layout options differ, look for any suggestion that mentions “bold headings” or “bullet points.” 💬 Example: *“Write a flyer heading ‘Neighbourhood Garage Sale – Saturday 9 am–2 pm’, include a brief intro and three featured items.”* You’ll know it worked when the returned text includes a clear heading, date, time, address, and a short description you can paste into a document.

## Step 5 — Print or export the flyer and share it
Select the flyer text, paste it into a word‑processing program (e.g., Microsoft Word or Google Docs), and use the built‑in **Print** command (usually a printer icon or Ctrl + P). You’ll see a print preview showing your flyer on a page. If the preview looks squashed, adjust the page margins or switch to **Landscape** orientation. If you prefer a digital copy, choose **Save as PDF** from the print dialog. You’ll know it worked when a printable page or PDF appears and you can either print it out or email it to neighbors.

## Common mistakes
- **Copy‑pasting the raw AI table into a word document without cleaning it up.** The table can turn into a jumbled block of text. Fix it by first pasting into a spreadsheet, then exporting as CSV or copying the cleaned table back into your document.  
- **Accepting the AI’s first price suggestion without checking local market rates.** Prices may be too high or low for your neighbourhood. Double‑check by looking at recent listings on local classifieds sites.  
- **Forgetting to include the sale’s address and contact number on the flyer.** The AI sometimes omits details if not asked. Add a line like “123 Maple St, Suburb XYZ – Call 0400 123 456” before printing.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You can quickly turn a cluttered garage into extra cash without spending hours writing lists or designing flyers yourself.  
- **For your business or work:** The same process can be adapted to catalogue inventory for a small retail pop‑up, saving time on product sheets.  
- **If you're just getting started:** The easiest first move is to open Meta AI and ask for a simple table – that single prompt gives you the backbone of the whole project.

## Try it now
Open Meta AI, type “Help me draft a garage‑sale flyer for this weekend,” and hit Enter. In under two minutes you’ll have a starter flyer to copy, edit, and print. Happy selling!
